A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work despite the changed title. Their main text, equations, figures, tables, and complete appendices are readable and support reliable comparison.

before.justification: Section 4 and Figure 1 report original numerical experiments comparing generalization error under optimal data poisoning and tailored Byzantine attacks; Appendix E.2 documents the construction.

after.justification: Section 4 and Figure 1 retain these original numerical results, with experimental details in Appendix F.2.

M1.justification: Appendix C.3 adds a Byzantine attack variant for SGD whose trigger uses previously observed gradients. Algorithm 1 also changes its GD attack condition from g1 <= C to g1 < C. The underlying SMEA, GD, and projected-SGD learning procedures remain unchanged.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same synthetic linear-loss construction under data poisoning and Byzantine failures. The new nonconvex material is theoretical and introduces no evaluated dataset or task.

E2.justification: Figure 1 retains the same attack comparisons and theoretical reference curves. Additional attack and aggregation names in Appendix I concern prior work or possible extensions, not newly evaluated comparators.

E3.justification: The numerical experiment retains n=15, m=1, T=5, gamma=C=1, and f=1 through 7. The worker identities, generalization-error measurement, and attack tolerance of 0.001 are also unchanged in v2 Appendix E.2 and v3 Appendix F.2.

E4.justification: Both versions retain the same analysis across corruption fractions. No empirical ablation, robustness experiment, error analysis, or case study is added; the new appendix analyses concern theoretical bounds.

E5.justification: Neither version reports experimental run counts, seed lists, confidence intervals, or error bars. The new reference to coupled runs sharing a seed is part of a mathematical proof, not experimental uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: Figure 1 uses the same embedded plot in both PDFs, retaining all empirical curves and their ordering. The numerical findings are unchanged; revisions to mathematical bounds are assessed under T1.

T1.justification: Theorem 3.3 and Appendix D.1 revise the intersection-contraction argument, changing the strongly convex poisoning bound's denominators from n-f to n-2f; corresponding excess-risk bounds are updated. Appendix C.3 adds an SGD lower-bound argument, and new Appendix E develops smooth nonconvex SGD stability bounds with supporting lemmas and proofs. These substantially revise and extend the theory.

C1.justification: The central separation between threat models remains. V3 narrows the introductory tightness summary from '(strongly) convex' to convex objectives, extends the stated Byzantine lower-bound coverage to SGD, and presents the existing stability-generalization equality as an independently useful contribution.

C2.justification: Appendix I substantially expands applicability and mechanism discussions: it conjectures tightness of the already existing low-corruption bound, discusses relaxing regularity assumptions, distinguishes extensions to other aggregation rules, and motivates clipping and threat-specific defenses. Section 3.2 also replaces the earlier general co-coercivity rationale with a more qualified interpretation.

D1.justification: Appendix F.2 corrects the numerical attack description to use a signed alpha_f chosen as small as possible, aligning it with the infimum-based pseudocode already present in v2. This clarifies implementation instructions without establishing a changed experiment; no code release or computing-resource information is added.

R1.justification: V3 adds relevant references, including work on nonconvex and nonsmooth stability, additional attack studies, and adaptive gradient clipping. Appendix I connects these works to possible extensions and more explicitly claims a theoretical justification for ZKPs, while retaining the central positioning against earlier optimization and generalization analyses.

P1.justification: V3 retitles the paper, rewrites the contribution summary and co-coercivity explanation, expands proof sketches, and brings the optimization-versus-generalization discussion into the main text. It adds an impact statement, but preserves the main section sequence and much of the existing prose.

P2.justification: The manuscript is comprehensively reformatted into an ICML proceedings layout, changing typography, front matter, affiliations, headers, and citation presentation. Table 1 moves into the introduction with a more specific caption. Figure 1 is rescaled and its caption changes from 'Stability' to 'Generalization Error'; an additional SGD pseudocode box appears.

improvement.justification: Correcting v2's intersection-contraction argument and overstrong bound improves the reliability of retained results, while revised explanations clarify their scope. However, the new SGD proof in Appendix C.3 uses an all-history trigger inconsistent with its 'at least once' argument and displays the negative factor 1-exp(k/2). These errors limit the benefit of the added theoretical scope.
